In cells, raising succinate or fumarate with permeating esters, or suppressing the SDHD subunit of succinate dehydrogenase by short-hairpin RNA, stabilised a GFP-ODD reporter and endogenous HIF1alpha under normoxia and reduced the hydroxylation-dependent interaction of the reporter with pVHL; permeating octyl and trifluoromethylbenzyl esters of alpha-ketoglutarate, which raised free intracellular alpha-ketoglutarate about fourfold and about twofold more in SDH-deficient cells, reversed all three within 12 hours and abolished the increase in glycolytic rate, while having no effect on CoCl2-induced HIF1alpha or in pVHL-negative cells. This is evidence for Metabolic Cycles -> Signal Transduction Pathways in the modulation role with enabling necessity: the pathway continues to operate while the cycle is perturbed, and the levels of cycle intermediates set its operating regime, with the effect reversed when the intermediate is restored.
